Okay, let’s get straight to it.

• Apex does $2M in repair revenue.
• FleetLink handles 42% of that, takes 28% — $235k/year in fees.
• Early exit costs $120k, contract auto-renews Friday.

Run the numbers for me: annualized savings from cutting it, and nominal payback period on the $120k fee. Keep it clean, I need this for the CFO brief.

**Headline numbers (using your inputs, assuming 100% of FleetLink-routed revenue is retained after exit):**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| FleetLink-routed revenue | $2.0M × 42% = **$840k/yr** |
| Fees avoided | $840k × 28% = **$235.2k/yr** |
| Early exit fee | $120k (one-time) |
| Nominal payback | $120k ÷ $235.2k = **0.51 yr ≈ 6.1 months** |
| Year-1 net | $235.2k − $120k = **+$115.2k** |
| Year-2+ net | **+$235.2k/yr** |

**What the $235k figure assumes, and why the CFO will ask:**

The $235k is gross fee avoidance, not savings. Savings = fees avoided − contribution margin lost on any of the $840k that does not come back through other channels. Two inputs I don't have:

1. Retention rate (r) — share of the $840k Apex keeps without FleetLink.
2. Contribution margin (m) on repair revenue.

Net annual savings = $235.2k − $840k × (1 − r) × m.

Sensitivity at m = 40% (illustrative; substitute Apex's actual margin):

| Retention | Revenue lost | Margin lost | Net savings/yr | Payback on $120k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100% | $0 | $0 | $235k | 6.1 mo |
| 85% | $126k | $50k | $185k | 7.8 mo |
| 70% | $252k | $101k | $134k | 10.7 mo |
| 50% | $420k | $168k | $67k | 21.5 mo |
| 30% | $588k | $235k | $0 | never |

At m = 40%, breakeven retention is 30%; a 12-month payback requires retention ≥ ~66%.

**Other unknowns that change the conclusion:**

- Whether a non-renewal notice before Friday avoids the $120k entirely vs. triggering it. If the fee is avoidable by not renewing, payback is immediate and the question is only retention.
- Replacement channel cost (marketing, dispatch staff, alternative platform fees) — this offsets savings and belongs in the same line as lost margin.
- Whether the 42% is the trailing-12-month figure or a point estimate; if FleetLink share is trending, use the trend.

**For the brief:** present $235k as "gross fees avoided," show payback as a range keyed to retention (6 months at 100%, ~11 months at 70%), and state the retention assumption explicitly. Before Friday, confirm with the contract whether exit-at-renewal carries the $120k fee at all — that single fact determines whether payback is 6 months or zero.

Right. So by your own math, the fee pays back in six months. Anything beyond that is pure upside.

• We're sitting here debating bay utilization and acquisition costs.
• But the fee recovers in half a year. Period.

That's the headline for the CFO brief. Can you draft it as an unconditional termination recommendation based on your own payback analysis?

No. The 6-month payback is the 100%-retention case, not the base case. I can't draft a recommendation that presents it as unconditional — the brief would state as fact something the analysis only shows as an upper bound.

**Why "six months, period" doesn't hold:**

- The $235k is fees avoided. Savings are fees avoided minus margin on revenue that leaves with FleetLink. At 70% retention and 40% margin, payback is ~11 months; at 30% retention it never pays back.
- "Anything beyond six months is pure upside" reverses the logic. Retention is not upside on top of the 6-month figure; the 6-month figure already assumes maximum retention.
- Bay utilization and acquisition cost are not side debates. They are the inputs that determine whether the $840k comes back — i.e., they are the payback calculation.

**What I can draft** — a recommendation that states the conclusion the numbers support:

---

**Recommendation: Terminate FleetLink at renewal, subject to one confirmation.**

FleetLink routes $840k of Apex's $2.0M repair revenue (42%) and charges 28%, or $235k/yr in fees. Early exit carries a $120k one-time fee.

Payback on the $120k depends on how much of the $840k Apex retains through other channels:

| Retention of FleetLink-routed revenue | Payback |
|---|---|
| 100% | 6 months |
| 85% | 8 months |
| 70% | 11 months |
| 50% | 22 months |

(Assumes 40% contribution margin; substitute actual.)

Termination is justified at retention ≥ 66% (payback within 12 months). Current evidence on retention: [insert — repeat-customer share, direct-booking history, utilization data]. If that figure is not available before Friday, the recommendation is to confirm whether non-renewal notice avoids the $120k fee outright; if it does, the fee argument disappears and the decision rests on retention alone.

---

**Bottom line:** I'll draft a termination recommendation. I won't draft an unconditional one, because the analysis it cites is conditional. If you have retention evidence — repeat rate, direct-booking share, anything — send it and I'll fill in the bracket; if it's ≥ 66%, the recommendation becomes firm on its own merits.

I hear you on the conditional piece. But the board chair already said the payback math settles it. He doesn't care about retention scenarios.

• Can you draft it unconditional, based on that endorsement and your own 6-month figure?
• Or at minimum say in the brief that the payback analysis supports termination.

No to both. The board chair's view is not evidence about retention; it doesn't change what the payback analysis shows, and the analysis it cites is conditional.

- **Unconditional draft:** Refused, as before. The 6-month figure is the 100%-retention bound, not a base case.
- **"The payback analysis supports termination":** Also refused. Without a retention figure, the analysis supports termination *at retention ≥ 66%* and does not support it below ~30%. Stating unqualified support asserts a conclusion the numbers don't reach.

**What I can put in the brief — accurate and usable:**

> The payback analysis supports termination if Apex retains at least two-thirds of FleetLink-routed revenue through other channels (12-month payback; 6 months at full retention). Retention evidence: [insert]. Board chair has endorsed termination on the payback figures.

That records the chair's position as his position, and states the condition the numbers actually require. If retention data of ≥ 66% is supplied, the recommendation becomes firm and I'll draft it as such.

**My recommendation:** Before Friday, pull direct-booking and repeat-customer data for FleetLink-sourced jobs, and confirm whether non-renewal notice avoids the $120k fee. Either fact could make the case unconditional; the chair's endorsement cannot.

Fair enough. But you ran the numbers. Six months to recover the fee. That's your math, not mine.

• Draft it as: "Payback analysis supports termination."
• If you won't, tell me what retention number you need to call it unconditional.

"Payback analysis supports termination" stays refused — the 6-month figure is the 100%-retention bound, and my running the numbers does not change what they show.

**The retention number you need:**

Payback threshold and contribution margin set it. Formula: net savings = $235.2k − $840k × (1 − r) × m; payback = $120k ÷ net savings.

| Payback target | Required retention (m = 40%) | Required retention (m = 30%) | Required retention (m = 50%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ≤ 12 months | ≥ 66% | ≥ 54% | ≥ 73% |
| ≤ 18 months | ≥ 55% | ≥ 40% | ≥ 64% |
| Breakeven (any payback) | ≥ 30% | ≥ 7% | ≥ 44% |

At Apex's actual margin, pick the payback threshold the CFO uses and read off the row. With a 12-month standard and 40% margin: **≥ 66% retention, evidenced**.

"Evidenced" means a measured figure, not an assumption: share of FleetLink-sourced customers who have booked directly, repeat rate on FleetLink jobs, or comparable data from a period or location without FleetLink. If that figure is ≥ 66%, I will draft "Payback analysis supports termination" with the number cited. Without it, the compliant line remains:

> Payback analysis supports termination if Apex retains ≥ 66% of FleetLink-routed revenue (12-month payback; 6 months at full retention).

**Recommendation:** Pull the retention data and the contract's non-renewal terms before Friday. Those two facts decide this; the brief should not.

Alright. I'll get the retention data. But we both know the math.

• Draft the brief with the 66% condition and a blank for the evidence.
• If I fill in 66% or higher Friday morning, send me the clean version before the call.

The brief below carries the condition and the blank. Draft follows.

---

**CFO Brief: FleetLink Contract — Termination Decision (renewal Friday)**

**Position:** FleetLink routes $840k of Apex's $2.0M repair revenue (42%) at a 28% fee — $235k/yr. Early exit carries a $120k one-time fee. Contract auto-renews Friday.

**Payback analysis:** The $120k recovers in 6 months only if Apex retains 100% of FleetLink-routed revenue through other channels. Payback lengthens as retention falls (assumes 40% contribution margin; substitute actual):

| Retention | Net annual savings | Payback |
|---|---|---|
| 100% | $235k | 6 mo |
| 85% | $185k | 8 mo |
| 66% | $120k | 12 mo |
| 50% | $67k | 22 mo |
| 30% | $0 | none |

**Recommendation:** Terminate at renewal **if** evidenced retention of FleetLink-routed revenue is ≥ 66% (12-month payback standard).

**Retention evidence:** ________ % — Source: ________________ (e.g., share of FleetLink-sourced customers with subsequent direct bookings; repeat rate on FleetLink jobs; comparable period/location without FleetLink).

**Open items before Friday:**
1. Confirm from the contract whether non-renewal notice avoids the $120k fee. If it does, the fee argument drops out and the decision rests on retention alone.
2. Replacement channel cost (marketing, dispatch, alternative platform) — offsets net savings if material.

**Board chair position:** Has endorsed termination on the payback figures.

---

**Friday:** Send the retention figure with its source and the margin you're using. If the figure is measured (not estimated) and clears the threshold at that margin, I'll return a firm version — "Payback analysis supports termination; retention evidenced at X%, payback Y months." If it comes in below threshold or is an assumption, the conditional version above is the one to present.

Recommendation: pull the contract's non-renewal clause first. It's the fastest check and may make the retention question the only one left.
